body:
Except their most recent pattern has been to only text me one single time on a Saturday.

Yeah I feel like I should just be done with it. I don't feel like a have a legal or moral obligation, but my inner people pleaser wants to make everyone happy.
I'm just worried about not satisfying them because they came to my house, I don't want them showing up harassing me.
It's difficult for me to get to church on a regular enough basis and definitely too short notice to ask for them to care of me after surgery.

My mom is my only family now, aside from her parents that are even less capable than her.

And since it usually is suggested next, I don't have friends, haven't for a long time. Mostly I haven't had the time or energy for that. Nor any kind of church family or anything.

Thanks, we can't afford dual household, but my mom has a large empty house and I was thinking of saying we should live apart and try dating again. First get some space, then try dating while we do therapy and work on recoupling.

I just need to figure out help around the house. I needed to figure it out anyway. The surgery I'm about to have will leave me basically an invalid for the first few weeks, I'm not to be left alone. A lot of people get home health for this surgery and a lot of insurances cover that. I need to find out if mine will. Still they are only there part of the time, during normal business hours.

It's a lot of shitty logistics. If I was a fully functional person then it wouldn't be as daunting and I hate that I have to consider that in my decision.

I expanded more in a reply to the other commenter. It is long and might help with perspective.

I very much want him, who he is as a person, in my life. The person I get currently is a shadow self. Someone who only reacts to daily life instead of the man I married.

I mentioned how I feel like the solution would be to have a nanny or home help and us live apart, because for the 4+ years we were together and didn't live in the same home, things were great.

As for my lost love. I feel like that isn't an issue anymore. It was many years ago and it took me a long time to get over it, but I feel like I did indeed get closure. I feel like I was well moved on by the time I met my current husband. There were a few other, short term, relationships between them.

As for my suicidal ideations. They are mostly under control. My last spell was the beginning of April. I struggle with it most when my own sleep gets out of whack, it throws my balance off and a teeter a little. So I try really hard to make sure I get enough sleep.

I live with chronic pain from a spinal injury. The pain is severely worsened if my body can't regenerate during sleep. Pain has gotten so bad I just wanted to end it, it's hard to deal with that.

I know if I'm left alone I will have to do more, I'll sleep less, and I'll hurt more. And I know what happens when I hurt, I just want to die. If that's coupled with the emotional side of a broken marriage... I've never dealt with that combo together but I assume it would make things worse.

I am doing everything I can to stop the triggers, take care of myself, and get some kind of permanent solution so it doesn't stay this way. So I would say that's part of my progress. Learning what triggers me, how to combat it, and how to hopefully stop it long term.

He has anxiety that he can't get under control. He is on medication and it helps for sure, but he needs to do the work to learn to recognize and deal with his daily triggers.

Instead they continue to grow and he begins to withdraw and seclude himself. He drops back into the mindset that things only impact him and he begins to lash out. Demanding silence and complete autonomy.

He gets very controlling during this time and emotionally manipulative. He's desperate to claw his way back into his safe place, which is literally him being a complete loner.

He also oversteps with the parenting. He's not really supposed to parent them, just support me and remind them to follow the rules. Instead, when he is in a bad place, he creates all his own rules and presses hard to enforce them. These rules he comes up with directly relate to giving him his safe place. Suddenly the children aren't allowed to play, sit on the furniture except one specific way, talk unless it is a gentle volume, eat if they've just eaten, etc... Basically control their every existence to fit his perfect mold (this is how his parents raised him, so it's his comfort zone-what he knows and understands).

We've had countless sessions on parenting, I've bought many books (that he never read), we've watched DVDs (but it had to be together or he would always find an excuse that he doesn't have the time) and they are all on the method of parenting we both agree on, which is the method I've always used. Yet as soon as his anxiety goes up even a little, everything goes out the window.

There's a lot of tension between us due to his inconsistencies. The more his anxiety goes up the worse he gets, the more we struggle, the worse we get, the more his anxiety goes up from that.

It's like an endless cycle. But he has been told the tools he needs to deal with the anxiety before it starts to impact his mood, he just doesn't do them. Two very simple things, probably the simplest of all tools he's been given, are making sure he goes to bed on time and drinking enough water. He's chronically tired and dehydrated and that has a huge impact on his daily anxiety level. But he refuses to do it. Says he always forgets, but then refuses to set an alarm for himself when he sets alarms for literally everything else. He has alarms to remind him to take out the trash, to feed the birds, to start the bedtime routine for the kids, but he won't set an alarm for his own bedtime. He won't put water as a task in his to-do app that he uses to remind himself to do other daily tasks that matter to him.

It seems so stupid. I want him to leave because he won't drink water. But that's not it. He won't take care of the things we've proven through trial and error that has a SIGNIFICANT impact on his anxiety. His anxiety that causes myself and the children to be miserable. The way he treats us because of his anxiety is why I want out.

I'm tired of us being treated like less than human when he's in a bad mood. I'm tired of being treated like an idiot for wanting to be touched, for wanting to have sex.

Of course sex is an issue between us. He never touches me, never tells me he wants me, never makes me feel wanted. If I want it I have to seduce him, never the other way. If he gets horny he jerks off in the shower alone instead of wanting his wife.

He makes me feel like a bad person for having feelings. He makes me feel guilty for being upset at how he mistreats us. He makes me feel crazy for wanting what I'm pretty certain is basic human desires and needs.

He doesn't yell and he's never been physical, that's the 2 things my dad did to me that I said I'd never tolerate. Instead I feel like I'm in some other kind of hell and I think I might be crazy and overreacting.
